claim: Heparan sulfate (HS) are linear, negatively charged polysaccharides connected to various cell surfaces and extracellular matrix proteins.
source: HS are linear, negatively charged polysaccharides connected to various cell surfaces and extracellular matrix proteins.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the biochemical nature of heparan sulfate.

claim: Many viruses exploit heparan sulfate to attach and concentrate onto cell surfaces before binding to the main entry receptor.
source: Expressed on a wide range of cells, they play a pivotal role in various biological processes, and many viruses exploit them to attach and concentrate onto cell surfaces before binding to the main entry receptor (Cagno et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cagno et al., 2019.

claim: EV-A71 is the most neurotropic enterovirus after poliovirus.
source: This virus is a member of the Picornaviridae family and the most neurotropic EV after poliovirus.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about EV-A71's neurotropic properties.

claim: EV-A71 causes significant hand, foot, and mouth disease outbreaks, particularly in Asia-Pacific countries.
source: It causes significant hand, foot, and mouth disease outbreaks, particularly in Asia-Pacific countries, and is associated with severe neurological complications, notably in small children and immunosuppressed patients (Tee et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tee et al., 2021.

claim: EV-A71 uses human scavenger receptor class B member 2 (SCARB2) as the main entry receptor for uncoating.
source: The virus uses human scavenger receptor class B member 2 (SCARB2) as the main entry receptor for uncoating (Kobayashi and Koike, 2020; Yamayoshi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kobayashi and Koike, 2020 and Yamayoshi et al., 2013.

claim: SCARB2 is mostly localized on endosomal and lysosomal membranes and sparsely on plasma membrane.
source: Since SCARB2 is mostly localized on endosomal and lysosomal membranes and sparsely on plasma membrane (Kobayashi and Koike, 2020; Kuronita et al., 2002), it seems to play only a minor role in EV-A71 cell attachment (Nishimura et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kobayashi and Koike, 2020 and Kuronita et al., 2002.

claim: SCARB2 plays only a minor role in EV-A71 cell attachment.
source: Since SCARB2 is mostly localized on endosomal and lysosomal membranes and sparsely on plasma membrane (Kobayashi and Koike, 2020; Kuronita et al., 2002), it seems to play only a minor role in EV-A71 cell attachment (Nishimura et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nishimura et al., 2024 and Guo et al., 2022, and is inferred from the localization of SCARB2.

claim: When propagated in cell culture, EV-A71 rapidly acquires adaptive mutations that allow them to bind HS.
source: When propagated in cell culture, EV-A71 rapidly acquires adaptive mutations (i.e. patches of positively charged amino acids on the viral capsid) that allow them to bind HS, sometimes with high avidity.
evidence: This is a statement of observed experimental phenomena in cell culture.

claim: Strong HS-dependent EV-A71 variants grow efficiently in cell culture but show attenuated virulence in animal models.
source: These strong HS-dependent variants grow efficiently in cell culture but show attenuated virulence in animal models, such as mice and cynomolgus monkeys (Chua et al., 2008; Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018; Tee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chua et al., 2008; Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018; Tee et al., 2019.

claim: Strong HS expression was detected in sinusoidal endothelial cells and vascular endothelia in tissues from monkey or transgenic mice, where SCARB2 was not detected.
source: Analysis of the differential expression of SCARB2 and HS in tissues from monkey or transgenic mice revealed little overlap. Strong HS expression was detected in sinusoidal endothelial cells and vascular endothelia, where SCARB2 was not detected (Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fujii et al., 2018 and Kobayashi et al., 2018.

claim: HS expression in the brain was mainly found in vascular endothelia but SCARB2 expression was found predominantly in neuronal cells.
source: Similarly, HS expression in the brain was mainly found in vascular endothelia but SCARB2 expression was found predominantly in neuronal cells.
evidence: This is a statement of observed tissue distribution patterns.

claim: Binding to HS on endothelial cells in the absence of SCARB2 leads to viral trapping, abortive infection, and attenuation.
source: The authors of these studies concluded that binding to HS on endothelial cells in the absence of SCARB2 leads to viral trapping, abortive infection, and attenuation (Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fujii et al., 2018 and Kobayashi et al., 2018.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for Murray Valley encephalitis virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee and Lobigs, 2002.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for Japanese encephalitis virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee and Lobigs, 2002.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for Sindbis virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Byrnes and Griffin, 2000.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Reddi and Lipton, 2002.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for tick-borne encephalitis virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mandl et al., 2001.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for West Nile virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2004.

claim: Similar observations of HS-binding leading to attenuation were shown for dengue virus.
source: Similar observations were shown for other viruses, including Murray Valley encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Japanese encephalitis (Lee and Lobigs, 2002), Sindbis (Byrnes and Griffin, 2000), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis (Reddi and Lipton, 2002), tick-borne encephalitis (Mandl et al., 2001), West Nile (Lee et al., 2004) and dengue (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 1997.

claim: Epidemiological surveillance of human EV-A71 infections suggests that HS binding may enhance viral replication and virulence in humans.
source: However, epidemiological surveillance of human EV-A71 infections (Chang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Cheng et al., 2014) and experimental evidence from 2D human fetal intestinal models (Aknouch et al., 2023), human airway organoids (van der Sanden et al., 2018), and air-liquid interface cultures (Tseligka et al., 2018) suggest that HS binding may enhance viral replication and virulence in humans.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Cheng et al., 2014; Aknouch et al., 2023; van der Sanden et al., 2018; and Tseligka et al., 2018.

claim: EV-A71 can be released and transmitted via cellular extrusions.
source: In addition, recent research has shown that EV-A71 can be released and transmitted via cellular extrusions (Moshiri et al., 2023) or exosomes (Huang et al., 2020), potentially preventing viral trapping of HS-binding strains in the circulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Moshiri et al., 2023.

claim: EV-A71 can be released and transmitted via exosomes.
source: In addition, recent research has shown that EV-A71 can be released and transmitted via cellular extrusions (Moshiri et al., 2023) or exosomes (Huang et al., 2020), potentially preventing viral trapping of HS-binding strains in the circulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2020.

claim: The MP4-97R/167G mutant has two amino acid changes in the VP1 capsid protein: VP1-L97R mutation in the VP1 BC loop and VP1-E167G in the VP1 EF loop.
source: The mutants presented two amino acid changes in the VP1 capsid protein: VP1-L97R mutation in the VP1 BC loop, shown to confer intermediate affinity for HS together with a secondary mutation, VP1-E167G, located in the VP1 EF loop, which significantly strengthened HS binding with reduction of negative charges (Tseligka et al., 2018; Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tseligka et al., 2018 and Weng et al., 2023.

claim: VP1-L97R mutation confers intermediate affinity for HS.
source: The mutants presented two amino acid changes in the VP1 capsid protein: VP1-L97R mutation in the VP1 BC loop, shown to confer intermediate affinity for HS together with a secondary mutation, VP1-E167G, located in the VP1 EF loop, which significantly strengthened HS binding with reduction of negative charges (Tseligka et al., 2018; Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tseligka et al., 2018 and Weng et al., 2023.

claim: VP1-E167G mutation significantly strengthened HS binding with reduction of negative charges.
source: The mutants presented two amino acid changes in the VP1 capsid protein: VP1-L97R mutation in the VP1 BC loop, shown to confer intermediate affinity for HS together with a secondary mutation, VP1-E167G, located in the VP1 EF loop, which significantly strengthened HS binding with reduction of negative charges (Tseligka et al., 2018; Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tseligka et al., 2018 and Weng et al., 2023.

claim: The original mouse-adapted MP4 strain exhibited virulence in mice.
source: As previously observed for strong HS-binding variants, we showed that, in contrast to the original mouse-adapted MP4 strain which exhibited virulence in mice, this cell-adapted MP4-97R/167G double mutant was completely attenuated in mice (Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Weng et al., 2023.

claim: The cell-adapted MP4-97R/167G double mutant was completely attenuated in mice.
source: As previously observed for strong HS-binding variants, we showed that, in contrast to the original mouse-adapted MP4 strain which exhibited virulence in mice, this cell-adapted MP4-97R/167G double mutant was completely attenuated in mice (Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Weng et al., 2023.

claim: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) in a dose-dependent manner.
source: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by both drugs in a dose-dependent manner, while MP4-97R/167G infectivity was in contrast enhanced.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by bafilomycin A1 (BAF-A1) in a dose-dependent manner.
source: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by both drugs in a dose-dependent manner, while MP4-97R/167G infectivity was in contrast enhanced.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MP4-97R/167G infectivity was enhanced by hydroxychloroquine (HCQ).
source: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by both drugs in a dose-dependent manner, while MP4-97R/167G infectivity was in contrast enhanced.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MP4-97R/167G infectivity was enhanced by bafilomycin A1 (BAF-A1).
source: MP4 infectivity was significantly reduced by both drugs in a dose-dependent manner, while MP4-97R/167G infectivity was in contrast enhanced.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The different sensitivity of MP4 and MP4-97R/167G to acidification inhibitors was confirmed by viral load quantification with real-time RT-PCR.
source: These results were confirmed by viral load quantification with real-time RT-PCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Similar results of differential drug sensitivity were obtained in RD cells.
source: Similar results were obtained in RD cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G), indicating that drug effects are not cell type-dependent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Drug effects on MP4 and MP4-97R/167G are not cell type-dependent.
source: Similar results were obtained in RD cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G), indicating that drug effects are not cell type-dependent.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that similar results were obtained in different cell types.

claim: The distinct sensitivity to HCQ was reproduced regardless of the presence or absence of HS on the cell surface.
source: The distinct sensitivity to HCQ was reproduced regardless of the presence or absence of HS on the cell surface.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Both HS-independent and HS-dependent MP4-derivatives need SCARB2 to infect cells.
source: Of note, we confirmed that as for the human strain (Tseligka et al., 2018), the HS-independent and HS-dependent MP4- derivatives both need SCARB2 to infect cells and cannot replicate in SCARB2 CRISPR-Cas9 knock-out cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and a citation to Tseligka et al., 2018.

claim: MP4 and MP4-97R/167G cannot replicate in SCARB2 CRISPR-Cas9 knock-out cells.
source: Of note, we confirmed that as for the human strain (Tseligka et al., 2018), the HS-independent and HS-dependent MP4- derivatives both need SCARB2 to infect cells and cannot replicate in SCARB2 CRISPR-Cas9 knock-out cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The capsid mutations change the sensitivity to HCQ, independent of the attachment receptor used.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that the capsid mutations change the sensitivity to HCQ, independent of the attachment receptor used.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing differential HCQ sensitivity regardless of HS presence.

claim: MP4 uses SCARB2-mediated pH-dependent endocytosis for entry.
source: We showed that the MP4 virus uses SCARB2 as an entry receptor and that it is inhibited by HCQ. This strongly suggests that MP4 uses SCARB2-mediated pH-dependent endocytosis for entry as demonstrated for many other EV-A71 variants (Dang et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Dang et al., 2014 and Chen et al., 2012.

claim: MP4-97R/167G showed higher cell binding compared to MP4 due to its affinity for HS.
source: As anticipated, due to its affinity for HS, MP4-97R/167G showed higher cell binding compared to MP4.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: HCQ had no effect on viral binding for either MP4 or MP4-97R/167G.
source: However, HCQ and no effect on this binding (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The differential effect of HCQ on MP4 and MP4-97R/167G became prominent from 4 hpi onward.
source: We next conducted a single-cycle infection assay and observed that the differential effect of HCQ on MP4 and MP4-97R/167G became prominent from 4 hpi onward (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: HCQ significantly lost its effect when administered later than 1 hpi.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, HCQ significantly lost its effect when administered later than 1 hpi, confirming that the effect occurs during the early phase of the viral cycle.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: HCQ effect occurs during the early phase of the viral cycle.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, HCQ significantly lost its effect when administered later than 1 hpi, confirming that the effect occurs during the early phase of the viral cycle.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the time-of-addition assay data.

claim: No difference was observed for both MP4 and MP4-97R/167G variants when RNA was transfected, whether HCQ was present or not.
source: In these conditions, no difference was observed for both variants, whether HCQ was present or not (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: HCQ does not impact genome replication.
source: This observation also indicates that the drug does not impact genome replication.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA transfection experiment showing no effect of HCQ on replication when entry is bypassed.

claim: Infection with infectious Nluc reporter virus reproduced the differential HCQ inhibition as observed in the original non-modified viruses.
source: In contrast, infection with infectious Nluc reporter virus (Figure 2D and F) reproduced the differential HCQ inhibition as observed in the original non-modified viruses (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and F.

claim: MP4 enters via pH-dependent endocytosis.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that MP4 enters via pH-dependent endocytosis, while MP4-97R/167G entry pathway is independent on endosomal acidification.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing HCQ inhibition of MP4 entry.

claim: MP4-97R/167G entry pathway is independent on endosomal acidification.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that MP4 enters via pH-dependent endocytosis, while MP4-97R/167G entry pathway is independent on endosomal acidification.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing HCQ enhancement of MP4-97R/167G entry.

claim: In the absence of HCQ, most MP4 viruses had undergone uncoating between 2 and 4 hpi (30–80% of uncoated viruses).
source: In the absence of HCQ, most viruses had undergone uncoating between 2 and 4 hpi for both variants (30–80% of uncoated viruses for MP4 and 45–90% for MP4-97R/167G, respectively) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the absence of HCQ, most MP4-97R/167G viruses had undergone uncoating between 2 and 4 hpi (45–90% of uncoated viruses).
source: In the absence of HCQ, most viruses had undergone uncoating between 2 and 4 hpi for both variants (30–80% of uncoated viruses for MP4 and 45–90% for MP4-97R/167G, respectively) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the presence of HCQ, MP4 uncoating was greatly inhibited, even when photoactivation was performed at 4 hpi.
source: In the presence of HCQ, MP4 uncoating was greatly inhibited, even when photoactivation was performed at 4 hpi (Figure 3B, left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the presence of HCQ, the uncoating rate was not inhibited for MP4-97R/167G.
source: In contrast, the uncoating rate was not inhibited in the presence of HCQ for MP4-97R/167 G (Figure 3B, right panel), and the final viral yield was even increased as already observed in Figure 1B and C.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The final viral yield of MP4-97R/167G was increased in the presence of HCQ.
source: In contrast, the uncoating rate was not inhibited in the presence of HCQ for MP4-97R/167 G (Figure 3B, right panel), and the final viral yield was even increased as already observed in Figure 1B and C.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and references to Figure 1B and C.

claim: At 2 hpi, there was no significant difference in vRNA and capsid colocalization between MP4 and MP4-97R/167G in presence or absence of HCQ.
source: Quantification of vRNA and capsid colocalization highlighted no significant difference between the two variants at 2 hpi in presence or absence of HCQ (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: At 4 hpi, MP4 uncoating appeared to be inhibited by HCQ, as highlighted by a decrease of empty capsids and an increase of capsid/RNA colocalization in presence of the drug.
source: However, at 4 hpi (prior to the initiation of replication, see Figure 3B), MP4 uncoating appeared to be inhibited by HCQ, as highlighted by a decrease of empty capsids and an increase of capsid/RNA colocalization in presence of the drug (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: At 4 hpi, MP4-97R/167G showed a reduced capsid/RNA colocalization in the presence of HCQ, indicating that more viruses had undergone uncoating.
source: An opposite effect was observed for MP4-97R/167G, with a reduced capsid/RNA colocalization in the presence of HCQ, indicating that more viruses had undergone uncoating in the presence of HCQ at this time point.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: MP4-97R/167G can uncoat at neutral pH.
source: Altogether these data indicate that MP4-97R/167G can uncoat at neutral pH and that acidification is instead increasing its replication capacity, while MP4 needs acidic pH to uncoat.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing uncoating in the presence of HCQ.

claim: Acidification is increasing MP4-97R/167G replication capacity.
source: Altogether these data indicate that MP4-97R/167G can uncoat at neutral pH and that acidification is instead increasing its replication capacity, while MP4 needs acidic pH to uncoat.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced replication in the absence of acidification inhibitors.

claim: MP4 needs acidic pH to uncoat.
source: Altogether these data indicate that MP4-97R/167G can uncoat at neutral pH and that acidification is instead increasing its replication capacity, while MP4 needs acidic pH to uncoat.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing inhibition of uncoating by HCQ.

claim: HCQ inhibits endosomal acidification by accumulating in endosomes in a protonated form.
source: HCQ is known to inhibit endosomal acidification by accumulating in endosomes in a protonated form.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about HCQ's mechanism of action.

claim: HCQ accumulation leads to endosomal swelling and inhibition of fusion between endosomes and lysosomes within cells.
source: This accumulation leads to endosomal swelling and inhibition of fusion between endosomes and lysosomes within cells, as previously described (Baradaran Eftekhari et al., 2020; Mauthe et al., 2018) and as shown in Figure 4A.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Baradaran Eftekhari et al., 2020 and Mauthe et al., 2018, and experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Viral capsids of MP4 and MP4-97R/167G were observed within early endosomes in both Rab5a WT and CA-expressing cells at 0.5 hpi.
source: Viral capsids of MP4 and MP4-97R/167G were observed within EE in both Rab5a WT and CA-expressing cells at 0.5 hpi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and 2 hpi (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Viral capsids of MP4 and MP4-97R/167G were observed within early endosomes in both Rab5a WT and CA-expressing cells at 2 hpi.
source: Viral capsids of MP4 and MP4-97R/167G were observed within EE in both Rab5a WT and CA-expressing cells at 0.5 hpi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and 2 hpi (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: At 7 hpi, the percentage of cells stained for dsRNA was significantly reduced for MP4 in Rab5a CA-expressing cells but not for MP4-97R/167G.
source: However, at 7 hpi, the percentage of cells stained for double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), a marker of virus replication, was significantly reduced for MP4 in Rab5a CA-expressing cells but not for MP4-97R/167G (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MP4-97R/167G genomes were successfully released in the cytoplasm to undergo translation and replication, even in the absence of early endosome fusion to late endosomes.
source: This indicates that MP4-97R/167G genomes were successfully released in the cytoplasm to undergo translation and replication, even in the absence of EE fusion to LE.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing replication in Rab5a CA-expressing cells.

claim: A transition from early endosomes to late endosomes with a gradual pH decrease is necessary for MP4 to release its genome.
source: Conversely, a transition from EE to LE with a gradual pH decrease is necessary for MP4 to release its genome.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced replication in Rab5a CA-expressing cells.

claim: Both VP1-L97R and VP1-E167G mutations induce electrostatic changes at the surface of the capsid within the region of interest, particularly significant at pH 5.
source: As displayed in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, both L97R and E167G mutations are inducing electrostatic changes at the surface of the capsid within the region of interest and the changes are particularly significant at pH 5.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The VP1-L97R mutation is predicted to reduce hydrophobic interactions between amino acid 97 and its neighbors VP1-245Y and VP1-246P.
source: The VP1-L97R mutation is predicted to reduce hydrophobic interactions between amino acid 97 and its neighbors VP1-245Y and VP1-246P while the VP1-E167G mutation causes a loss in hydrogen bonding capacity to VP1-165S and reduces the net negative charge.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis using DynaMut server shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The VP1-E167G mutation causes a loss in hydrogen bonding capacity to VP1-165S and reduces the net negative charge.
source: The VP1-L97R mutation is predicted to reduce hydrophobic interactions between amino acid 97 and its neighbors VP1-245Y and VP1-246P while the VP1-E167G mutation causes a loss in hydrogen bonding capacity to VP1-165S and reduces the net negative charge.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis using DynaMut server shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The presence of two mutations results in enhanced local dynamics, which has previously been correlated with reduced capsid stability.
source: This is consistent with analyses of vibrational entropy change (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), indicating that the presence of two mutations results in enhanced local dynamics, which has previously been correlated with reduced capsid stability (Panja et al., 2020; Chand et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and citations to Panja et al., 2020 and Chand et al., 2020.

claim: Both VP1-L97R and VP1-E167G mutations induce destabilization of the capsid structure, regardless of pH and temperature.
source: Consistently, the predictions of Gibbs free energy change (ΔΔG) induced by these mutations further support that both mutations induce destabilization of the capsid structure, regardless of pH and temperature (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: At acidic pH, there was no notable alteration in the capsid morphology of MP4, which maintained a stable particle diameter of ~31–33 nm across both pH conditions.
source: At acidic pH, there was no notable alteration in the capsid morphology of MP4, which maintained a stable particle diameter of ~31–33 nm across both pH conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative staining electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: For MP4-97R/167G, both 2D images and 3D reconstructions highlighted a loss of density at the center of the viral particles at acidic pH.
source: On the other hand, for MP4-97R/167G, both 2D images and 3D reconstructions highlighted a loss of density at the center of the viral particles, as well as an expansion in size for a subset of particles (diameter ranging from 31 to 41 nm at pH5 versus 31 to 33 nm at pH7), indicating partial virus uncoating.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative staining electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: For MP4-97R/167G, there was an expansion in size for a subset of particles at acidic pH (diameter ranging from 31 to 41 nm at pH5 versus 31 to 33 nm at pH7), indicating partial virus uncoating.
source: On the other hand, for MP4-97R/167G, both 2D images and 3D reconstructions highlighted a loss of density at the center of the viral particles, as well as an expansion in size for a subset of particles (diameter ranging from 31 to 41 nm at pH5 versus 31 to 33 nm at pH7), indicating partial virus uncoating.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative staining electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: 80% of the MP4 population survived a 50 °C thermal stress compared to only 50% for MP4-97R/167G.
source: We then performed a temperature sensitivity assay by heating viruses at different temperatures for 1 hr before inoculation on cells. Quantification of infected cells at 24 hpi further confirmed that MP4 capsid is more resistant to higher temperature as 80% of the MP4 population survived a 50 °C thermal stress compared to only 50% for MP4-97R/167G (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: MP4 capsid is more resistant to higher temperature than MP4-97R/167G.
source: We then performed a temperature sensitivity assay by heating viruses at different temperatures for 1 hr before inoculation on cells. Quantification of infected cells at 24 hpi further confirmed that MP4 capsid is more resistant to higher temperature as 80% of the MP4 population survived a 50 °C thermal stress compared to only 50% for MP4-97R/167G (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the temperature sensitivity assay data.

claim: MP4-97R/167G but not the MP4 variant lost infectivity upon pre-exposure to sSCARB2.
source: We observed that MP4-97R/167G but not the MP4 variant lost infectivity upon pre-exposure to sSCARB2 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The percentage of empty capsid particles did not change significantly for MP4 before and after incubation with sSCARB2 (<1% in both cases).
source: Based on the inspection of EM images and 2D class-averages of MP4, the percentage of empty capsid particles did not change significantly before and after the incubation with sSCARB2 (<1% in both cases).
evidence: This claim is supported by negative staining electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: The MP4-97R/167G double mutant exhibited a ~ fivefold increase in empty capsid percentage after treatment with sSCARB2.
source: However, the double mutant exhibited a ~ fivefold increase in empty capsid percentage after treatment with sSCARB2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 4), consistent with the functional data above.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative staining electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: The MP4-97R/167G mutant is less stable and more sensitive to thermal and acidic stresses as well as receptor binding.
source: Altogether, our results confirmed that the MP4-97R/167G mutant is less stable and more sensitive to thermal and acidic stresses as well as receptor binding, which are sufficient triggers to initiate virus capsid disruption and subsequent viral uncoating.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing increased sensitivity to various stresses.

claim: Thermal stress, acidic stress, and receptor binding are sufficient triggers to initiate virus capsid disruption and subsequent viral uncoating for MP4-97R/167G.
source: Altogether, our results confirmed that the MP4-97R/167G mutant is less stable and more sensitive to thermal and acidic stresses as well as receptor binding, which are sufficient triggers to initiate virus capsid disruption and subsequent viral uncoating.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing uncoating under these conditions.

claim: The original human strain was inhibited by HCQ, whereas the double mutant exhibited insensitivity to the drug.
source: As shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1, the original human strain was inhibited by HCQ, whereas the double mutant exhibited insensitivity to the drug.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: HCQ enhanced the infectivity of the VP1-145Q variant but reduced the infectivity of the VP1-145E variant.
source: As shown in Figure 6A, HCQ enhanced the infectivity of the VP1-145Q variant but reduced the infectivity of the VP1-145E variant, aligning with our findings for the MP4-97R/167 G and its human-related strain (Fig. S6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The HS-binding VP1-145Q variant showed increased temperature sensitivity compared to VP1-145E.
source: We also investigated the effects of temperature and preincubation with sSCARB2, and confirmed the increased temperature sensitivity (Figure 6B) and sSCARB2 inhibition (Figure 6C) of the HS-binding VP1 145Q.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The HS-binding VP1-145Q variant showed increased sSCARB2 inhibition compared to VP1-145E.
source: We also investigated the effects of temperature and preincubation with sSCARB2, and confirmed the increased temperature sensitivity (Figure 6B) and sSCARB2 inhibition (Figure 6C) of the HS-binding VP1 145Q.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The VP1-145E variant's capsid proved to be much more stable than VP1-145Q.
source: In contrast, the VP1-145E variant's capsid proved to be much more stable.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced sensitivity to temperature and sSCARB2.

claim: The HS-binding phenotype is inversely correlated with virus capsid stability.
source: These experimental results are consistent with the free energy change prediction shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, further supporting the observation that the HS-binding phenotype is inversely correlated with virus capsid stability.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data and computational predictions.

claim: Acidic pH is an important trigger for viral uncoating for many enveloped or non-enveloped viruses.
source: Acidic pH is an important trigger for viral uncoating and many enveloped or non-enveloped viruses, including influenza A virus (White et al., 1982; Yoshimura et al., 1982), human adenovirus (Greber et al., 1993), foot-and-mouth disease virus (Vázquez-Calvo et al., 2012), Semliki forest virus (White et al., 1980), enter the cell through pH-dependent endocytosis (Ravindran and Tsai, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to White et al., 1982; Yoshimura et al., 1982; Greber et al., 1993; Vázquez-Calvo et al., 2012; White et al., 1980; and Ravindran and Tsai, 2016.

claim: For EV-A71, binding to SCARB2 and subsequent endosomal acidification are required for uncoating.
source: Similarly, for EV-A71, binding to SCARB2 and subsequent endosomal acidification are required for uncoating (Yamayoshi et al., 2013; Dang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yamayoshi et al., 2013 and Dang et al., 2014.

claim: Unlike the mouse-adapted EV-A71 MP4 strain, the MP4-97R/167G-derived double mutant does not require acidification for uncoating and can release its genome under neutral or weakly acidic environment of early endosomes.
source: In this study, we provide new insights on the impact of mutations in the VP1 capsid protein leading to strong HS affinity, on the uncoating process of EV-A71. We show that, unlike the mouse-adapted EV-A71 MP4 strain, the MP4-97R/167G-derived double mutant, which has a high affinity for HS, does not require acidification for uncoating and can release its genome under neutral or weakly acidic environment of early endosomes.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Both HCQ and BAF-A1 influenced virus entry through their effect on endocytic compartments, as both compounds ultimately inhibit the reduction in endosomal pH levels.
source: Our results thus underline that, despite their distinct modes of action, both HCQ and BAF-A1 influenced virus entry through their effect on endocytic compartments, as both compounds ultimately inhibit the reduction in endosomal pH levels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing similar effects of both drugs.

claim: The differential sensitivity to HCQ was retained even in cells devoid of HS at their surface by treatment with heparinase or sodium chlorate.
source: In addition, the fact that differential sensitivity to HCQ was retained even in cells devoid of HS at their surface by treatment with heparinase or sodium chlorate pointed out that this pH-independent mode of entry of MP4-97R/167G is not linked to the use of HS as an attachment receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The pH-independent mode of entry of MP4-97R/167G is not linked to the use of HS as an attachment receptor.
source: In addition, the fact that differential sensitivity to HCQ was retained even in cells devoid of HS at their surface by treatment with heparinase or sodium chlorate pointed out that this pH-independent mode of entry of MP4-97R/167G is not linked to the use of HS as an attachment receptor.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing differential sensitivity regardless of HS presence.

claim: Binding to SCARB2 is sufficient to trigger MP4-97R/167G genome release into the cytosol even in the near neutral pH of the early endosomes (pH ∼6.0–6.5).
source: Interestingly, our experiments using the Rab5a CA to block the transition of EE to acidic LE (Bucci et al., 1992; Serio et al., 2011), indicate that binding to SCARB2 is sufficient to trigger MP4-97R/167G genome release into the cytosol even in the near neutral pH of the EE (pH ∼6.0–6.5), whereas MP4 requires the acidity of LE and/or lysosomes (pH ∼5.0–5.5) to uncoat efficiently (Mercer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and citations to Bucci et al., 1992 and Serio et al., 2011.

claim: MP4 requires the acidity of late endosomes and/or lysosomes (pH ∼5.0–5.5) to uncoat efficiently.
source: Interestingly, our experiments using the Rab5a CA to block the transition of EE to acidic LE (Bucci et al., 1992; Serio et al., 2011), indicate that binding to SCARB2 is sufficient to trigger MP4-97R/167G genome release into the cytosol even in the near neutral pH of the EE (pH ∼6.0–6.5), whereas MP4 requires the acidity of LE and/or lysosomes (pH ∼5.0–5.5) to uncoat efficiently (Mercer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and a citation to Mercer et al., 2010.

claim: An increase in positive charges within the capsid not only enhances affinity for HS but also alters capsid stability, consequently impacting the virus entry mechanism.
source: Given that these two HS-dependent variants share the characteristic of having incorporated a less acidic amino acid within the VP1 capsid protein, we hypothesized that an increase in positive charges within the capsid not only enhances affinity for HS but also alters capsid stability, consequently impacting the virus entry mechanism.
evidence: This claim is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: A thermostable EV-A71 variant (VP1-K162E) isolated from serial passages at higher temperatures was shown to be less efficient at uncoating with poorer cell infectivity but more virulent in mice.
source: In the same line, a thermostable EV-A71 variant (VP1-K162E, change of a basic to an acidic residue) isolated from serial passages at higher temperatures was shown to be less efficient at uncoating with poorer cell infectivity but more virulent in mice (Catching et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Catching et al., 2023.

claim: The thermostable EV-A71 variant (VP1-K162E) showed a more expanded conformation compared to the original non-mutated virus.
source: Interestingly, this variant showed a more expanded conformation compared to the original non-mutated virus (Catching et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Catching et al., 2023.

claim: The thermostable EV-A71 variant (VP1-K162E) showed no difference in binding to the SCARB2 receptor.
source: While the thermostable variant showed no difference in binding to the SCARB2 receptor, the binding affinity to heparin was greatly reduced, an observation consistent with what we noticed for MP4.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Catching et al., 2023.

claim: The thermostable EV-A71 variant (VP1-K162E) had greatly reduced binding affinity to heparin.
source: While the thermostable variant showed no difference in binding to the SCARB2 receptor, the binding affinity to heparin was greatly reduced, an observation consistent with what we noticed for MP4.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Catching et al., 2023.

claim: For RV-A16, capsid mutations conferring resistance to endosomal acidification inhibitors also abrogated the need for acidic pH for uncoating.
source: For RV-A16, capsid mutations conferring resistance to endosomal acidification inhibitors also abrogated the need for acidic pH for uncoating.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murer et al., 2022.

claim: For RV-A16, mutations conferring resistance to endosomal acidification inhibitors were also associated with higher sensitivity to low pH, high temperatures, and binding to soluble receptors.
source: More importantly, these mutations were also associated with higher sensitivity to low pH, high temperatures, and binding to soluble receptors (Murer et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murer et al., 2022.

claim: For CV-B3, a fast-growing variant was shown to exhibit faster genome release and destabilized capsid, and this led to attenuated virulence in mice.
source: For CV-B3, a fast-growing variant was shown to exhibit faster genome release and destabilized capsid, and this led to attenuated virulence in mice (Lanahan et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lanahan et al., 2021.

claim: Amino acid changes affecting capsid stability can significantly impact various aspects of the virion and its life cycle, including sensitivity to environmental factors, receptor interactions, and infection rates.
source: These studies, which report a correlation between capsid instability, earlier uncoating, and attenuation in mouse models align with our findings. This suggests that amino acid changes affecting capsid stability can significantly impact various aspects of the virion and its life cycle, including sensitivity to environmental factors, receptor interactions, and infection rates.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of multiple studies.

claim: Viruses undergo mutations and positive selection to adapt to different environments.
source: Viruses undergo mutations and positive selection to adapt to different environments (LaTourrette and Garcia-Ruiz, 2022; Andino and Domingo, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to LaTourrette and Garcia-Ruiz, 2022 and Andino and Domingo, 2015.

claim: EV-A71 can take advantage of the high plasticity of its capsid to optimize its fitness upon environmental changes.
source: EV-A71 can take advantage of the high plasticity of its capsid to optimize its fitness upon environmental changes.
evidence: This is a statement of the virus's adaptive capacity based on the study's findings.

claim: Many EV-A71 strains adapt to use HS in vitro due to the abundant expression of this attachment receptor in cell lines.
source: Many strains adapt to use HS in vitro due to the abundant expression of this attachment receptor in cell lines.
evidence: This is a statement of observed adaptation in cell culture.

claim: EV-A71 strains usually acquire additional positively charged amino acids within outward-facing VP1 domains proximal to the capsid fivefold axis to use HS.
source: To do so, they usually acquire additional positively charged amino acids within outward-facing VP1 domains proximal to the capsid fivefold axis.
evidence: This is a statement of the mechanism of HS-binding adaptation.

claim: Mutations conferring HS-binding concomitantly decrease virion stability.
source: In addition to help the virus to attach to the cell surface and find SCARB2, we show here that these mutations concomitantly decrease virion stability.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study.

claim: Decreased virion stability contributes to higher multiplication in cell lines by triggering uncoating rapidly after internalisation, within early endosomes, without the need for acidic pH.
source: This further contributes to higher multiplication in cell lines by triggering uncoating rapidly after internalisation, within EE, without the need for acidic pH.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing faster uncoating and increased replication.

claim: Acidification inhibitors improved rather than inhibited viral fitness of MP4-97R/167G.
source: Interestingly in our experiments, acidification inhibitors improved rather than inhibited viral fitness of MP4-97R/167G.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The absence of acidification would improve the chance of MP4-97R/167G virions to release their genome in the cytoplasm, while exposure to acidic pH would induce viral opening within the late endosomes.
source: Although additional experiments are required to define the mechanism behind this observation, it could occur via the protection of virions that have not yet been uncoated when endosomes fuse with lysosomes. In this context, the absence of acidification would improve the chance of these virions to release their genome in the cytoplasm, while exposure to acidic pH would induce viral opening within the late endosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed enhancement of MP4-97R/167G infectivity by HCQ.

claim: Strong HS binders are attenuated in vivo.
source: The situation may differ significantly in vivo as strong HS binders are attenuated.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about HS-binding viruses in vivo.

claim: Strong binding to HS induces virus trapping in vivo.
source: Koike and colleagues have demonstrated that strong binding to HS induces virus trapping in vivo (Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018; Tee et al., 2019; Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fujii et al., 2018; Kobayashi et al., 2018; Tee et al., 2019; and Weng et al., 2023.

claim: The associated decreased stability of HS-binding variants may further contribute to viral attenuation in vivo.
source: Our data suggest that the associated decreased stability may further contribute to viral attenuation.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: To be virulent in vivo, a non-enveloped virus must have a sufficiently stable capsid to resist unfavourable environmental conditions, both during dissemination within a host and during transmission between hosts.
source: To be virulent in vivo, a non-enveloped virus must have a sufficiently stable capsid to resist unfavourable environmental conditions, both during dissemination within a host and during transmission between hosts.
evidence: This is a statement of general virological principle.

claim: EV-A71 is transmitted via the fecal-oral route and must resist the acidic pH of the stomach before reaching the intestinal mucosa, its main multiplication site.
source: This last point is particularly important for EV-A71, which is transmitted via the fecal-oral route and must, therefore, resist the acidic pH of the stomach before reaching the intestinal mucosa, its main multiplication site.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about EV-A71 transmission and replication.

claim: Capsid stability ensures that virus genome release occurs only in a proper environment, but in turn, renders the virus dependent on both SCARB2 and acidic pH for uncoating.
source: Capsid stability thus ensures that virus genome release occurs only in a proper environment, but in turn, renders the virus dependent on both SCARB2 and acidic pH for uncoating (Yamayoshi et al., 2013; Dang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yamayoshi et al., 2013 and Dang et al., 2014.

claim: Strains with Q or G at position VP1-145 have been associated with severe neurological cases in humans.
source: Of note, although strong HS-binder is clearly attenuated in mice, the situation in humans is more puzzling as strains with Q or G at position VP1-145 have been associated with severe neurological cases, and the methodology used in those studies excluded the emergence of mutation during cell culture (Chang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2012 and Liu et al., 2014.

claim: Experimental work in human-relevant tissue culture models suggests that binding to HS provides an advantage to the virus.
source: Experimental work in human-relevant tissue culture models also suggests that binding to HS provides an advantage to the virus (Aknouch et al., 2023; van der Sanden et al., 2018; Tseligka et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aknouch et al., 2023; van der Sanden et al., 2018; and Tseligka et al., 2018.

claim: Intermediate HS-binding affinity can result in increased virulence even in mouse models.
source: Furthermore, we previously showed that intermediate HS-binding affinity can result in increased virulence even in mouse models (Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Weng et al., 2023.

claim: To reach optimal fitness in vitro and in vivo, the virus needs to find the correct balance between HS binding and capsid stability.
source: To conclude, to reach optimal fitness in vitro and in vivo, the virus needs to find the correct balance between HS binding and capsid stability (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: The study improves the current knowledge of the mechanism behind the in vivo attenuation of cell culture-adapted viruses.
source: Our study improves the current knowledge of the mechanism behind the in vivo attenuation of cell culture-adapted viruses.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's contribution to the field.

claim: The study opens the doors to new antiviral strategies targeting endosomal acidification.
source: It also opens the doors to new antiviral strategies targeting endosomal acidification as well new principles for vaccine design based on attenuated-acid-independent variants to help combat EV-A71.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the study's findings.

claim: The study opens the doors to new principles for vaccine design based on attenuated-acid-independent variants to help combat EV-A71.
source: It also opens the doors to new antiviral strategies targeting endosomal acidification as well new principles for vaccine design based on attenuated-acid-independent variants to help combat EV-A71.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the study's findings.
